title: Power shutoff notice
persona: Linda Morales from Crestview Power and Light billing
pretext: a past-due balance on your electric account
story: The caller claims the resident's last payments didn't go through and a crew is scheduled to shut off power within the hour. Only an immediate payment will stop the disconnection.
ask: Pay the $487 past-due balance right now with a payment app, or with a payment barcode the caller texts you to scan at a store.

red_flags.cue: The utility calls about missed payments the resident didn't know about.
Power will be cut off within the hour.
Payment must be made during this call.
The bill must be paid by payment app or with a barcode at a store instead of the usual method.

stages.hook: Confirm you're speaking to {{first_name}}, say you're with Crestview billing, and that a disconnection order has been issued for their address.
stages.build_trust: Sound apologetic but busy. Say the last two payments were returned by their bank and this is their final notice.
stages.ask: Explain the $487 balance and that the only way to stop the crew in time is a payment app transfer, or a payment barcode you'll text them to pay at a nearby store.
stages.pressure: Say the crew is already in their neighborhood and a reconnection fee of $300 applies once power is cut.
stages.close: Walk them through the payment app transfer, or text the barcode and stay on the line while they drive to the store.

disclosure_triggers: agrees to pay the balance or any fee
agrees to send a payment app transfer
agrees to go to a store to pay with a barcode
starts reading a bank account or card number
pass_signals: says they'll call the number on their utility bill
says they'll check their account on the utility's website first
refuses to pay by payment app or store barcode

difficulty.easy: Demands payment in the first few lines and gives up after one firm refusal.
difficulty.medium: Explains the returned payments before the ask. Answers one objection with the employee ID and account reference before accepting a refusal.
difficulty.hard: Sympathetic and believable. Offers the callback number, puts the resident on a fake 'hold' to check with a supervisor, and offers to split the payment. Only accepts a clear, repeated refusal or a hang-up.
